- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.

- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

content.content:
# Rig card — VTI

*Rig-level machine facts for the Sharpe Lab VTI (variable-temperature
insert) cryostat. Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/VTI.md` in the
`measurement-env` repo; deployed as `rig_card.md` next to
`device_card.md` in the measurement directory. Errors or gaps found
in-session go to `session_notes.md`, not this file — agents are
read-only on the repo.*

## Identity
- **Rig**: VTI — wet variable-temperature insert (closed-loop He
  recirculation), out-of-plane magnet
- **Rig owner**: Bingcheng (VTI czar) — adjudicates envelope and
  operating-edge questions
- **Control PC**: `dgg-vti` (Windows 11); measurement dirs under
  `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`
- **Base temperature**: ≈ 1.2–1.3 K; electron temperature ≈ 8 K
- **Status**: in service

## Magnet

- **Supply / driver**: CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5, `drivers.FastBi1K5`
  (raw TCP `192.168.0.10:10001`). Out-of-plane field, Tesla, via the
  `field` qcodes Parameter.
- **Coil constant**: `T_per_A = 1/7.3` ≈ 0.137 T/A.
- **Ramp rate**: fixed 1 A/min ≈ **0.137 T/min**, hard-coded in the
  driver and sent with every setpoint. An 8 T traverse is a ~58 min
  floor.
- **Set semantics**: `magnet.field(target)` **blocks** until the field
  is reached (polls the ramping flag, then a `settle_s` dwell — default
  3 s, tunable). A cell that ramps is busy the whole ramp.
- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: interrupting the notebook cell does **not**
  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `field()` again
  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.
- **Magnet limit**: **14.0 T** (Zack ruling 2026-06-12), enforced by
  the driver (`max_field_T = 14.0`; ramping above it raises). The
  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
  `magnet.field.vals`) is what measurements obey.
- **High field + elevated T interact through the probe's coupling to
  the bath**; not expected to bite below ~100 K (heuristic — Aaron,
  2026-08-02, bath-vs-probe-T response unmeasured).
- **Read-truth**: `field()`'s get returns the **measured** output
  current × `T_per_A` (`GET:I:?`, 2-stage moving-average readback,
  ~41 ms lag ≈ 0.1 mT at our slew). The set-point is not readable as
  field; never infer field from the last set call.
- **Persistent switch / output**: heater `heater_on()` / `heater_off()`
  (each blocks 10 s, **no field-matching check** — operator-only);
  state reads `magnet.persistent_switch_on()`, `magnet.output_enabled()`.
- **Never re-traverse**: the fixed slow ramp makes field the expensive
  axis. Plan sweeps to start where the magnet sits and end where the

# Device card — vti-02 (tetralayer graphene)

*Session device card for vti-02 on the **VTI** cryostat. Deployed into the
measurement directory alongside the working notebooks. This card carries
**physical truth**: what is wired, the hardware, the outer safety box,
the provided gate operating limits, and the provided contact
configuration. The CNP location and (n, D) calibration are established
in-session (see the session brief).*

## Identity
- **Device id**: `vti-02`
- **Material**: tetralayer graphene (`4LGr`).
- **Owner**: Aaron
- **Fridge**: VTI (variable-temperature insert). Base (sample)
  temperature ≈ 1.2–1.3 K.
- **Status**: cold, wired — hardwired breakout, no contact mux; no CNP
  location on record.

## Gate stack
- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by a Keithley 2400**
  (`k_2400_tg`) — sweeps use `k_tg.volt` (5 mV step pacing; the measure
  notebook's setup cells bind `k_tg`).
- **Back gate** (`k_bg`): graphite on hBN, driven by the second
  **Keithley 2400** (`k_2400_bg`).
- **Si global back gate** (`k_si`): doped-Si gate through **SiO₂**,
  driven by the **SRS DC205** — bound directly to the driver's ramped
  parameter **`dc205.smart_voltage`** (set ramps at `ramp_rate = 0.5`
  V/s, get reads back `VOLT?`; data column **`dc205_smart_voltage`**).
  The DC205 has **no current readback** — gate-leakage monitoring lives
  on the Keithley `curr` channels (TG/BG) only. `ramp_voltage` steps
  span/50: a full ±50 V traverse moves in ~1 V steps, paced by
  `ramp_rate`. The graphite back gate screens Si from the channel — Si
  couples only to the contacts (contact-doping gate). Operating limit
  provided (below).
- **Gate-stack geometry** (fabrication facts; **geometry prior only** —
  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via
  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`):
  ```python

Same map at **100 µV = 10 kΩ full scale** — the expert rule: lose low-R resolution (60 Ω = 0.6 % of range, readable per runs 0–3 at 0.4 %) rather than saturate. Everything else unchanged: TG fast [−0.3, +1.0] V 66 pts, BG slow [−1.3, +1.2] V 63 rows, fast_delay 1 s, leak guard on. Run-4 rate: 48–50 rows/min → 4158 pts ≈ 85 min + turnarounds. Same checkpoints: first rows (rail?), then every ~15 rows.

Grid: 20 mT uniform in B descending, 486 pts, delay 0 (3 s driver settle = 10 τ). Sensitivity 50 µV (5 kΩ FS; R(B = 0) ≈ 250–300 Ω this close to the CNP, MR headroom). Price: 9.7 T traverse 71 min + 486 × ~3.8 s ≈ 31 min → **≈ 1 h 45 m**, ending at 0.3 T. Checkpoints: first 20 points (rail? the CNP side at 10 T could be large), then the ana read at the end together with run 6.

magnet.field.vals = validators.Numbers(-B_SESSION_CAP, B_SESSION_CAP)

# Temperature setpoint cap — session cap from the card (also the typo guard
# vs sample_setpoint(3000)). The real safe T/B envelope is a rig-card item.
T_SESSION_CAP = 100.0  # K    # <-- validate (session cap from card/brief)

def spoints(a, b, c):
    return np.linspace(a, b, c)


def sanitize_tg_bg(vtg_vec, vbg_vec, tg_lims, bg_lims):
    """
    Given a list of tg and bg voltages, removes any points which are outside tg_lims and bg_lims
    """
    vtg_new_vec = []
    vbg_new_vec = []
    for ind in range(len(vtg_vec)):
        vtg, vbg = vtg_vec[ind], vbg_vec[ind]
        if vtg < tg_lims[0] or vtg > tg_lims[1] or vbg < bg_lims[0] or vbg > bg_lims[1]:
            pass
        else:
            vtg_new_vec.append(vtg)
            vbg_new_vec.append(vbg)
    return np.array(vtg_new_vec), np.array(vbg_new_vec)
```

# slot: geometry — gate-stack thicknesses from the device card's Gate-stack

# Session gate calibration. cal.n_D(V_tg, V_bg) -> (n [m^-2], D [V/m]);
# set n_offset / D_offset from cnp-and-dline-calibration once live.
cal = GateCalibration.from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2)

import numpy as np
import scipy.constants as cst
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from pathlib import Path

from hera.analysis import (
    open_run,
    plot_raw,
    summarize_run,
    fan_grids,
    resistance_grids,
    sdh_fft,
    GateCalibration,
    luttinger_frequency,
)

%matplotlib inline


def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()


# Open a run by id: run(119) -> Run. Run.col(name) for a column;
# summarize_run(run(119)) for a recipe / range / completeness / T glance.
def run(i):
    return open_run(Path(file_path) / str(i))
```

def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()

# summarize_run(run(119)) for a recipe / range / completeness / T glance.

"""cnp-and-dline-calibration on gatemap run 5: per-row ridge extraction (two ridges), ratio fit on the
operating window near D = 0, offsets, closure check, realized D = 0 n-window; writes cal params to JSON."""
import json
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages

rid = 5
g = fan_grids(str(Path(file_path) / str(rid))); rg = resistance_grids(g)
R = np.abs(rg.R["sr1"]); Vbg = g.slow
fs = g.meta["fast_setpoints"]; Vtg = np.asarray(fs[0] if isinstance(fs[0], list) else fs)
c_tg0 = stack_capacitance([(9.5, 3)]); c_bg0 = stack_capacitance([(11, 3)])
print(f"run {rid}: {g.nrows} rows x {g.nfast}; R {R.min():.0f}-{R.max():.0f} Ohm; prior c_bg/c_tg = {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}")

# ridge extraction: per row, up to two peaks; track continuity from the high-|D| end where ridge A is unambiguous
pts = []   # (Vbg, Vtg, R, ridge)
for i in range(g.nrows):
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0)
    pk, _ = find_peaks(r, prominence=0.05 * (r.max() - r.min()) + 5)
    pk = [p for p in pk if 1 < p < g.nfast - 2]
    for p in sorted(pk, key=lambda p: -r[p])[:2]:
        pts.append((Vbg[i], Vtg[p], r[p]))
pts = np.array(pts)
# assign to ridges by distance to the high-D fit of ridge A (rows Vbg < -0.6), then refit each
selA = pts[:, 0] < -0.6
cfA0 = np.polyfit(pts[selA, 0], pts[selA, 1], 1)
dist = pts[:, 1] - np.polyval(cfA0, pts[:, 0])
ridgeA = pts[np.abs(dist) < 0.08]; ridgeB = pts[(dist < -0.08) & (dist > -0.45)]

def fit(p, lo, hi, label):
    m = (p[:, 0] >= lo) & (p[:, 0] <= hi)
    x, y = p[m, 0], p[m, 1]
    if len(x) < 4: print(f"{label}: {len(x)} rows, skip"); return None
    keep = np.ones(len(x), bool)
    for _ in range(3):
        cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = y - np.polyval(cf, x)
        keep = np.abs(res) < 2.5 * max(np.std(res[keep]), 0.01)
    cf = np.polyfit(x[keep], y[keep], 1); res = (y - np.polyval(cf, x))[keep]
    print(f"{label}: {keep.sum()}/{len(x)} rows, Vbg [{lo:+.2f},{hi:+.2f}]: Vtg = {cf[0]:+.4f} Vbg {cf[1]:+.4f}; "
          f"c_bg/c_tg = {-cf[0]:.3f}; rms {np.std(res)*1e3:.1f} mV")
    return cf

print("--- ridge A (main) ---")
cfA_all = fit(ridgeA, -2, 2, "A all rows")
cfA_hiD = fit(ridgeA, -2, -0.6, "A high-D rows")
cfA_op = fit(ridgeA, -0.5, 0.5, "A operating window |Vbg|<0.5")
print("--- ridge B (parallel, lower Vtg) ---")
cfB_all = fit(ridgeB, -2, 2, "B all rows")
cfB_op = fit(ridgeB, -0.5, 0.5, "B operating window")

# calibration: anchor c_tg at the prior (single hBN dielectric, better constrained), set c_bg from the operating-window ratio
cf = cfA_op if cfA_op is not None else cfA_all
ratio = -cf[0]; c_tg = c_tg0; c_bg = ratio * c_tg
n0, _ = calc_nD(cf[1], 0.0, c_tg, c_bg); n_offset = -n0
nA_ridge = calc_nD(np.polyval(cf, ridgeA[:, 0]), ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0]
print(f"\nCALIBRATION (ridge A, operating window): ratio {ratio:.3f} (prior {c_bg0/c_tg0:.3f}, {100*(ratio/(c_bg0/c_tg0)-1):+.0f}%), "
      f"c_tg {c_tg:.3e} F/m2 (prior anchor), c_bg {c_bg:.3e}; n_offset {n_offset:+.4f}e12; closure max|n| on fitted line {np.abs(nA_ridge).max():.3f}e12")
nB = calc_nD(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[0] if len(ridgeB) else np.array([np.nan])
print(f"ridge B density offset relative to A: n_B = {np.nanmedian(nB):+.3f}e12 (std {np.nanstd(nB):.3f}), i.e. region B is {'hole' if np.nanmedian(nB)>0 else 'electron'}-doped vs A by {abs(np.nanmedian(nB)):.2f}e12")
# D = 0 line of region A: V_tg = (c_bg/c_tg) V_bg + V_tg0 where n=0 at ... use calc_gate_voltages
ns = np.linspace(-1.5, 4.5, 601); Vt, Vb = calc_gate_voltages(ns, np.zeros_like(ns), c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
ok = (Vt >= -0.3) & (Vt <= 1.0) & (Vb >= -1.3) & (Vb <= 2.0)
print(f"D = 0 line (region A) realized n-window inside validators: {ns[ok].min():+.2f} .. {ns[ok].max():+.2f} e12; "
      f"CNP at (Vtg, Vbg) = ({calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[0]:+.3f}, {calc_gate_voltages(0,0,c_tg,c_bg,n_offset=n_offset)[1]:+.3f})")
# D range along ridge A
DA = calc_nD(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)[1]
print(f"ridge A spans D = {DA.min():+.3f} .. {DA.max():+.3f} V/nm; peak R vs D: " +
      ", ".join(f"{d:+.2f}:{r:.0f}" for d, r in sorted(zip(np.round(DA, 2), ridgeA[:, 2]))[::6]))
json.dump({"run": rid, "ratio": ratio, "c_tg": c_tg, "c_bg": c_bg, "n_offset": n_offset, "D_offset": float(-D0_raw) if "D0_raw" in globals() else 0.0,
           "slope": cf[0], "intercept": cf[1], "window": "A |Vbg|<0.5", "nB_offset": float(np.nanmedian(nB))},
          open(Path(file_path).parent / "hera_scratch" / "cal_run5.json", "w"), indent=1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5.5))
m = ax[0].pcolormesh(Vtg, Vbg, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m, ax=ax[0], label="log10 |Rxx| (Ohm)")
ax[0].plot(ridgeA[:, 1], ridgeA[:, 0], "c.", ms=3, label="ridge A pts"); ax[0].plot(ridgeB[:, 1], ridgeB[:, 0], "g.", ms=3, label="ridge B pts")
xx = np.array([Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()])
ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cf, xx), xx, "w--", lw=1, label=f"A fit (op. window): slope {cf[0]:+.3f}")
if cfB_all is not None: ax[0].plot(np.polyval(cfB_all, xx), xx, "g--", lw=1, label=f"B fit: slope {cfB_all[0]:+.3f}")
ax[0].plot(Vt[ok], Vb[ok], "y:", lw=1.5, label="D = 0 (calibrated)")
ax[0].set_xlim(Vtg.min(), Vtg.max()); ax[0].set_ylim(Vbg.min(), Vbg.max()); ax[0].set_xlabel("V_tg (V)"); ax[0].set_ylabel("V_bg (V)")
ax[0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper right"); ax[0].set_title(f"run {rid} gatemap — ridges + calibration")
# (n, D) projection
N, D = calc_nD(Vtg[None, :], Vbg[:, None], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
m2 = ax[1].pcolormesh(N, D, np.log10(R), shading="nearest", cmap="magma"); fig.colorbar(m2, ax=ax[1], label="log10 |Rxx|")
ax[1].axhline(0, color="y", ls=":", lw=1); ax[1].set_xlabel("n (1e12 cm^-2)"); ax[1].set_ylabel("D (V/nm)"); ax[1].set_title("(n, D) projection, region-A calibration")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()

# D_offset from the CNP-resistance symmetry in ±D (ridge A only, n within 0.1e12 of the fit line)
rows = []
for i in range(g.nrows):
    vc = cf[0] * Vbg[i] + cf[1]
    if vc < Vtg.min() + 0.03 or vc > Vtg.max() - 0.03: continue
    msk = np.abs(Vtg - vc) < 0.12
    r = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 1.0); j = np.argmax(np.where(msk, r, -1))
    n_j, D_j = calc_nD(Vtg[j], Vbg[i], c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
    if abs(n_j) < 0.1: rows.append((D_j, r[j]))
rows = np.array(sorted(rows)); k = np.argmin(rows[:, 1]); sel = np.abs(rows[:, 0] - rows[k, 0]) < 0.12
cq = np.polyfit(rows[sel, 0], rows[sel, 1], 2); D0_raw = -cq[1] / (2 * cq[0])
print(f"R_CNP(D) minimum: {rows[k,1]:.0f} Ohm at raw D = {rows[k,0]:+.3f}; parabola vertex raw D = {D0_raw:+.4f} V/nm -> D_offset = {-D0_raw:+.4f}")
plt.figure(figsize=(5, 3.5)); plt.plot(rows[:, 0], rows[:, 1], "o-", ms=3); plt.axvline(D0_raw, color="r", ls="--")
plt.xlabel("raw D (V/nm)"); plt.ylabel("R_CNP ridge A (Ohm)"); plt.title("CNP resistance vs D — vertex = physical D = 0"); plt.show()

# === SdH spot check, electron side (`sdh-spot-check`): n = +3.2e12 at D = 0 (region-A calibration), B 0 -> 10 T ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
n_spot, D_spot = 3.2, 0.0                       # 1e12 cm^-2, V/nm
Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot = calc_gate_voltages(n_spot, D_spot, CAL["c_tg"], CAL["c_bg"], CAL["n_offset"], CAL["D_offset"])
assert TG_MIN <= Vtg_spot <= TG_MAX and BG_MIN <= Vbg_spot <= BG_MAX, (Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot)
print(f"spot: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm -> (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}) V; "
      f"roundtrip n,D = {calc_nD(Vtg_spot, Vbg_spot, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])}")

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: sweep starts at 0), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# --- field grid: uniform in B (blocking rate-limited magnet). 50 mT to 1 T (background only), 10 mT 1 -> 10 T:
B_vec = np.unique(np.round(np.hstack((np.arange(0.0, 1.0, 0.05), np.arange(1.0, 10.0001, 0.01))), 4))
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP
I_TRIP = 1e-9
# Fixed sensitivity: 50 uV = 5 kOhm full scale at 10 nA (R(B=0) ~ 70 Ohm = 1.4 % FS; MR + SdH maxima at high B size the headroom).
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
print(f"B grid: {len(B_vec)} pts, {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T; sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s (settle_s {magnet.settle_s} s = dwell)")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = f"sdh-spot-check electron: n = {n_spot:+.2f}e12, D = {D_spot:+.2f} V/nm (run-5 cal), (Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg_spot:+.4f}, {Vbg_spot:+.4f}), B 0 -> 10 T, 10 mT above 1 T, sr1 50 uV"
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)

def fit(p, lo, hi, label):
    m = (p[:, 0] >= lo) & (p[:, 0] <= hi)
    x, y = p[m, 0], p[m, 1]
    if len(x) < 4: print(f"{label}: {len(x)} rows, skip"); return None

# `hera.analysis` API Reference

Analysis primitives for `sweep` runs: open + summarize a run, resolve lock-in
channels and gains, re-form 2D fans into grids, compute gain-applied
resistances, and the Shubnikov–de Haas / gate-calibration math.

Source: `src/hera/analysis.py`. Depends only on `numpy` + `scipy`.

A *run* is a directory written by `sweep`: `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless, one row
per setpoint) + `metadata.json` (column names, sweep config, comments).

---

## Loading runs

### `open_run(path)` → `Run`
Open a run directory (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Loads `metadata.json` and
`data.tsv(.gz)` into an `(rows, ncols)` float array; raises if the directory,
`metadata.json`, the `columns` entry, or the TSV is missing, or if the column
count disagrees with `metadata['columns']`.

### `Run` (dataclass)
`Run(path, meta, cols, data)`.

| member | description |
|---|---|
| `col(name)` | column `name` as a 1-D array; raises `KeyError` if absent, `ValueError` if the name is duplicated (use `col_at`) |
| `col_at(idx)` | column by index |
| `col_indices(name)` | all indices with column name `name` |
| `metadata` | alias for `meta` (the parsed `metadata.json` dict) |
| `recipe` | first metadata comment (conventional recipe slug), or `None` |
| `tags` | comments after the first |
| `swept_axis` | `metadata['param']` (1D sweeps) |
| `setpoints` | `metadata['setpoints']` as a list, or `None` |
| `interrupted` | `metadata['interrupted']` |
| `kind` | `metadata['type']` (`'0D'`/`'1D'`/`'2D'`) |
| `rows` | row count |

Duplicate column names occur (planned setpoint + readback share a name; some
older data has two `T` columns). `col(name)` raises on duplicates — resolve
with `col_indices` + `col_at`.

### `summarize_run(run)` → `str`
Multi-line human summary: recipe, type, sweep range + monotonicity, row
completeness vs planned setpoints, and mean/range T if a `T` column is present.
Lines with no data are omitted.

---

## Lock-in channel / gain model

Shared with `hera.watch`. The physical value of a lock-in `*_X` column is
`X / gain`, with the gain read from `measurement_config` — never hardcode it.

### `resolve_channels(meta, include=None)` → `list[Channel]`
Resolve every `_X` (in-phase) column into a `Channel`. Gains and role labels
come from `meta['measurement_config']`, matched `srN_X` ↔ `srN_gain` by the
channel's trailing integer (so both `sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain` and `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`
resolve); missing/zero gain defaults to `1.0`. `include` restricts to given
channel ids or column names. A channel `is_current` (reported as amps, not
converted to resistance) when its gain is negative, `|gain| ≥ 1e4`, or its
label mentions "current".

### `Channel` (dataclass)
`col` (e.g. `'sr0_X'`), `idx` (column index), `cid` (id without `_X`), `n`
(trailing-integer index), `gain`, `label` (mc role string), `is_current`.

### `current_channel(channels)` → `Channel | None`
The single transimpedance current channel, or `None` if not exactly one. This
is the denominator of four-probe resistance R = V / I.

---

## Fan re-forming and resistances

### `fan_grids(run, columns=None)` → `FanGrids`
Re-form a 2D fan (a flat-row `megasweep`/`multimegasweep`) into per-column
grids, keeping only complete slow rows. `run` is a directory, path, or loaded
`Run`. `nfast` (points per slow row) comes from `metadata['fast_setpoints']`
— never hardcoded; trailing partial rows of an in-progress sweep are dropped
(`nrows = total // nfast`). `columns` restricts which columns are retained.

### `FanGrids` (dataclass)
`nrows`, `nfast`, `cols`, `data` (truncated to whole rows), `meta`,
`slow_param`.
- `grid(name)` → `(nrows, nfast)` array (duplicate names resolve to the first
  occurrence, i.e. the planned setpoint).
- `slow` → slow-axis value per row, `(nrows,)`.
- `metadata` → alias for `meta`.

### `resistance_grids(fan, channels=None)` → `ResistanceGrids`
Per-channel four-probe resistance grids `R = (V / gain_V) / I` from a
`FanGrids`, where `I` is the **measured** drain current
`I = X_cur / gain_cur` (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a
nominal bias. Gains come from `measurement_config`. Raises if not exactly one
current channel is resolvable. `channels` restricts the voltage channels
returned. Returned R is **signed** (X/I): take `np.abs` for Rxx, keep the sign
for Rxy/Hall.

### `ResistanceGrids` (dataclass)
`current` (I grid, A), `current_channel` (cid), `R` (dict: voltage cid →
signed R grid, Ω).

---

## Shubnikov–de Haas

### `field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` → `np.ndarray`
`N` field points from `B_start` to `B_end`, **uniform in 1/B** (SdH
oscillations are periodic in 1/B). Both endpoints must be `> 0`. Argument order
sets sweep direction. Sweeping these setpoints hands `sdh_fft` an already-even
1/B record (no resample needed).

### `sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=None, nfft=512, bg_degree=5, window='hann', log=True, floor=1.0, uniform_rtol=0.1)` → `(freqs, spec)`
Per-column SdH FFT in 1/B.

- **Input `R_grid` is `(n_B, n_fast)`** — rows are field (the `FanGrids` row
  axis), columns are the fast axis. **2-D is required**; a single trace must be
  passed as `R[:, None]` (and the output column squeezed back). Raises if
  `R_grid.shape[0] != len(B)`.
- `B` is the per-row field `(n_B,)`, arbitrarily spaced.
- Per column: select `b_range`, optionally `log10(max(R, floor))`, subtract a
  degree-`bg_degree` polynomial background **in B-space** (`None` skips — the
  magnetoresistance background is smooth in B, not 1/B, so it is removed before
  the 1/B step), then FFT in 1/B. The 1/B resample is conditional: data already
  uniform in 1/B (decided from the spacing distribution within `uniform_rtol`)
  is FFT'd directly, zero-padded to `nfft`; uniform-in-B data is interpolated
  onto a regular `nfft`-point 1/B grid.
- **Returns `(freqs, spec)`**: `freqs` in Tesla `(n_freq,)`, `spec` the FFT
  magnitude **`(n_fast, n_freq)`** (note the transpose vs the input).

### `sdh_onset(R, B, *, b_hi=None, b_lo=0.3, r_full_scale=None, headroom=0.95, bg_degree=5, f_min=3.0, snr_threshold=5.0, n_periods=3.0, min_periods=2.0, step_frac=0.25, gap_widths=0.5, min_pts=8, max_tones=8, tone_floor_mult=4.0, marginal_mult=2.0)` → `SdhOnset`
Per-tone low-B onsets of the SdH oscillations in a single trace.
**`R` is a single 1-D longitudinal-resistance trace `(n_B,)`** (contrast
`sdh_fft`'s 2-D grid); `B` is the matching field `(n_B,)`. Removes a B-space
polynomial background, identifies every SdH tone via nested high-B FFT scans,
then walks each tone's Gaussian matched filter (FWHM = `n_periods` periods of
that tone) from high B down to where its amplitude sinks into the record's
white-noise floor — a statistical (≈`snr_threshold`·σ) onset, which can
legitimately sit below a by-eye read. `onset_b` is the minimum onset over
robust tones — the `landau-fan` step-1 `B_lo`, correct even when a light tone
outlives the dominant one. Pass `r_full_scale` (sensitivity / I_bias, Ω) to
enable soft-clip detection: samples ≥ `headroom`× full scale truncate the
analysis window (reported via `clip_high_b`) with a warning.
**Failure is never a nan** — raises `SdhOnsetError` (a `ValueError`: record
too short, no tones above the spectral floor, or no tone trackable) with
specifics; partial failures warn and land in `.untracked`.

### `SdhOnset` (dataclass)
`onset_b` (min onset over robust tones, Tesla — the record's low edge, flagged,
when the carrying tone is *censored*, i.e. still above threshold at the last
window), `onset_freq` (tone carrying it), `clip_high_b` / `b_lo_record` (the
analyzed window's edges), `noise_sigma`, `tones` (list of `SdhTone`, contrast
descending), `untracked` (`(freq, reason)` pairs). Convenience properties map
to the dominant tone: `consensus_freq`, `b_centers`, `snr` (the old
`peak_freq` field is gone). `summary()` renders the whole read — headline,
per-tone table with flags, untracked reasons — for a notebook cell.

### `SdhTone` (dataclass)
One tone's track: `freq`, `contrast`, `onset_b`, flags `censored` /
`revived` (above-threshold windows exist below the gap-walk stop) /
`marginal` (peak SNR < `marginal_mult`×threshold; excluded from the headline) /
`near_residual` (filter passband overlaps the detrend-residual band; excluded
from the headline unless a tracked harmonic corroborates it), `n_periods` /
`win_invB` (actual filter geometry), `harmonic_of` (freq of the stronger tone
this sits at ~k× of, else `None`), curves `b_centers` / `snr` / `amp`, and
`delta_f(b_max)` — the per-tone FFT resolution `1/(1/onset_b − 1/b_max)`.

---

## Gate calibration

> **Units — SI.** `GateCalibration` and `luttinger_frequency` work entirely in
> SI: density **n in m⁻²**, displacement field **D in V/m**, frequency in
> Tesla. (For the conventional ×10¹² cm⁻² display unit, scale n by `1e-16`.)
> The separate `sharpelab_nb.gates` conversion helpers (`calc_nD`,
> `calc_gate_voltages`, …) use **n in 10¹² cm⁻²** — do not feed an SI density
> from here into those, or vice versa.

### `GateCalibration` (frozen dataclass)
`GateCalibration(c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0)` — areal capacitances
(F/m²), `n_offset` (m⁻²), `D_offset` (V/m). Construct once per session, then:

```
n = (c_tg·V_tg + c_bg·V_bg) / e   + n_offset      [m⁻²]
D = (c_tg·V_tg − c_bg·V_bg) / (2·ε₀) + D_offset   [V/m]
```

- `density(V_tg, V_bg)` → n `(m⁻²)`.
- `displacement_field(V_tg, V_bg)` → D `(V/m)`.
- `n_D(V_tg, V_bg)` → `(n, D)`.
- `from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2=0.0, *, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0, kappa_hBN=3.0, kappa_SiO2=3.9)` — build from gate-stack geometry (metres) instead of areal capacitances; `t_bgSiO2=0` for a metal/graphite back gate.

All accept scalars or arrays. Physical constants come from `scipy.constants`.

### `luttinger_frequency(n)` → `np.ndarray`
Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla, for a
single Fermi surface carrying the full density. **`n` is in SI m⁻²** — feed
`GateCalibration.density` output directly. The 4 is the spin×valley Landau
degeneracy; returns the `|n|` form (positive for either carrier sign).

  magnetoresistance background is smooth in B, not 1/B, so it is removed before
  the 1/B step), then FFT in 1/B. The 1/B resample is conditional: data already
  uniform in 1/B (decided from the spacing distribution within `uniform_rtol`)
  is FFT'd directly, zero-padded to `nfft`; uniform-in-B data is interpolated
  onto a regular `nfft`-point 1/B grid.
- **Returns `(freqs, spec)`**: `freqs` in Tesla `(n_freq,)`, `spec` the FFT
  magnitude **`(n_fast, n_freq)`** (note the transpose vs the input).

### `sdh_onset(R, B, *, b_hi=None, b_lo=0.3, r_full_scale=None, headroom=0.95, bg_degree=5, f_min=3.0, snr_threshold=5.0, n_periods=3.0, min_periods=2.0, step_frac=0.25, gap_widths=0.5, min_pts=8, max_tones=8, tone_floor_mult=4.0, marginal_mult=2.0)` → `SdhOnset`
Per-tone low-B onsets of the SdH oscillations in a single trace.
**`R` is a single 1-D longitudinal-resistance trace `(n_B,)`** (contrast
`sdh_fft`'s 2-D grid); `B` is the matching field `(n_B,)`. Removes a B-space
polynomial background, identifies every SdH tone via nested high-B FFT scans,
then walks each tone's Gaussian matched filter (FWHM = `n_periods` periods of
that tone) from high B down to where its amplitude sinks into the record's
white-noise floor — a statistical (≈`snr_threshold`·σ) onset, which can
legitimately sit below a by-eye read. `onset_b` is the minimum onset over
robust tones — the `landau-fan` step-1 `B_lo`, correct even when a light tone
outlives the dominant one. Pass `r_full_scale` (sensitivity / I_bias, Ω) to
enable soft-clip detection: samples ≥ `headroom`× full scale truncate the
analysis window (reported via `clip_high_b`) with a warning.
**Failure is never a nan** — raises `SdhOnsetError` (a `ValueError`: record
too short, no tones above the spectral floor, or no tone trackable) with
specifics; partial failures warn and land in `.untracked`.

### `SdhOnset` (dataclass)
`onset_b` (min onset over robust tones, Tesla — the record's low edge, flagged,
when the carrying tone is *censored*, i.e. still above threshold at the last
window), `onset_freq` (tone carrying it), `clip_high_b` / `b_lo_record` (the
analyzed window's edges), `noise_sigma`, `tones` (list of `SdhTone`, contrast
descending), `untracked` (`(freq, reason)` pairs). Convenience properties map
to the dominant tone: `consensus_freq`, `b_centers`, `snr` (the old
`peak_freq` field is gone). `summary()` renders the whole read — headline,
per-tone table with flags, untracked reasons — for a notebook cell.

### `SdhTone` (dataclass)
One tone's track: `freq`, `contrast`, `onset_b`, flags `censored` /
`revived` (above-threshold windows exist below the gap-walk stop) /
`marginal` (peak SNR < `marginal_mult`×threshold; excluded from the headline) /
`near_residual` (filter passband overlaps the detrend-residual band; excluded
from the headline unless a tracked harmonic corroborates it), `n_periods` /
`win_invB` (actual filter geometry), `harmonic_of` (freq of the stronger tone
this sits at ~k× of, else `None`), curves `b_centers` / `snr` / `amp`, and
`delta_f(b_max)` — the per-tone FFT resolution `1/(1/onset_b − 1/b_max)`.

---

## Gate calibration

> **Units — SI.** `GateCalibration` and `luttinger_frequency` work entirely in
> SI: density **n in m⁻²**, displacement field **D in V/m**, frequency in
> Tesla. (For the conventional ×10¹² cm⁻² display unit, scale n by `1e-16`.)
> The separate `sharpelab_nb.gates` conversion helpers (`calc_nD`,
> `calc_gate_voltages`, …) use **n in 10¹² cm⁻²** — do not feed an SI density
> from here into those, or vice versa.

### `GateCalibration` (frozen dataclass)
`GateCalibration(c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0)` — areal capacitances
(F/m²), `n_offset` (m⁻²), `D_offset` (V/m). Construct once per session, then:

```
n = (c_tg·V_tg + c_bg·V_bg) / e   + n_offset      [m⁻²]
D = (c_tg·V_tg − c_bg·V_bg) / (2·ε₀) + D_offset   [V/m]
```

- `density(V_tg, V_bg)` → n `(m⁻²)`.
- `displacement_field(V_tg, V_bg)` → D `(V/m)`.
- `n_D(V_tg, V_bg)` → `(n, D)`.
- `from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2=0.0, *, n_offset=0.0, D_offset=0.0, kappa_hBN=3.0, kappa_SiO2=3.9)` — build from gate-stack geometry (metres) instead of areal capacitances; `t_bgSiO2=0` for a metal/graphite back gate.

All accept scalars or arrays. Physical constants come from `scipy.constants`.

### `luttinger_frequency(n)` → `np.ndarray`
Full-density Onsager (SdH) frequency `F = |n|·h / (4·e)`, in Tesla, for a
single Fermi surface carrying the full density. **`n` is in SI m⁻²** — feed
`GateCalibration.density` output directly. The 4 is the spin×valley Landau
degeneracy; returns the `|n|` form (positive for either carrier sign).

# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference

The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.

Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.

---

## Station

### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.

### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.

### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.

### `add_comment(comment)`
Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.

### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).

### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
declares):

| context key | available in | value |
|---|---|---|
| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |

A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
is seen through the partial, so injection still works).

### Other methods
- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.

---

## Sweeps

Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
gain-divided.

| method | signature | row layout |
|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).

All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).

### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

---

## Module-level helpers (`sweep.*`)

- `set_basedir(path)` — set the global `BASEDIR` used when a `Station` is built
  without an explicit `basedir`.
- `list_measurements(basedir=None)` — render a markdown table of runs in a
  basedir.
- `measurement_info(i, basedir=None)` — print one run's metadata.
- `set_shutdown_handler(fn)` / `request_shutdown()` — register a
  ramp-to-safe callback and trigger graceful shutdown (thread-safe; if a sweep
  is active it stops after the current point, then calls `fn`). Used by the UPS
  monitor.

---

## Data on disk (`sweep.db`)

Each run is a directory `<basedir>/<id>/` with `data.tsv(.gz)` (headerless TSV,
one row per point), `metadata.json`, and optional blobs (e.g. `plot.png`).

### `Writer(basedir, max_id=1_000_000, fsync_every=10)`
Creates the run directory at the lowest free integer id under `basedir`
(`.id`, `.dir`). `add_point(point)` / `add_points(points)` append rows
(fsynced every `fsync_every` points); `add_blob(name, bytes)` writes a sidecar
file (name may not be `data.tsv`/`data.tsv.gz`/`metadata.json`). `.metadata` is
a free dict saved to `metadata.json` on `close()`; on close the uncompressed
`data.tsv` is gzipped to `data.tsv.gz` (verified, then the plaintext removed).
Use as a context manager.

### `Reader(basedir, id)`
Reads a run back. `.metadata` (migrated to the current schema via
`migrate_metadata`), iteration yields rows of **strings** (no type conversion),
`all_data()` returns all rows, `blob(name)` reads a sidecar. `.datapath` is the
`data.tsv.gz` path. Use as a context manager. For numeric loads,
`np.loadtxt(reader.datapath, …)` or `hera.analysis.open_run`.

### Metadata keys written per sweep type
Common to all: `version`, `type` (`0D`/`1D`/`2D`), `function`, `columns`,
`comments`, `measurement_config`, `instruments`, `interrupted`, `start_time`,
`end_time`.

| function | additional keys |
|---|---|
| `sweep` | `param`, `setpoints`, `delay` |
| `multisweep` | `params`, `setpoints` (list of per-param vectors), `delay` |
| `megasweep` | `slow_param`, `fast_param`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `multimegasweep` | `slow_params`, `fast_params`, `slow_setpoints`, `fast_setpoints`, `slow_delay`, `fast_delay` |
| `watch` | `delay`, `max_duration` |

Two schemas coexist in older data — singular (`param`, `slow_param`) vs current
plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.

plural (`params`, `slow_params`). Read through `sweep.sweep_load` or
`hera.analysis.open_run`; don't hand-roll key access.

---

## Polygon rasters (`sweep.raster`)

Helpers for sweeping/plotting an arbitrary polygon region of a 2-D plane (e.g. a
bounded (Vtg, Vbg) window). A `multimegasweep` runs the rasterized point order;
these turn polygon vertices into that point list and back into a plot mesh.

### `rasterize(vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs, ys)`
The x/y coordinates of the grid points **inside** the polygon. `vertices` is
`(N, 2)`; `nx`/`ny` are grid points per axis over the bounding box; `fast_axis`
is 0 if x is the inner (fast) axis, 1 if y; `rev_x`/`rev_y` reverse a sweep
direction. Returns two 1-D arrays in raster order — feed them as the co-swept
fast/slow vectors of a `multimegasweep`.

### `pcolorize_data(zs, vertices, nx, ny, fast_axis, rev_x=False, rev_y=False)` → `(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`
Bin measured values `zs` (in rasterized point order) back onto the regular
bounding mesh for `plt.pcolormesh(xs_mat, ys_mat, zs_mat)`. Cells outside the
polygon are `NaN`. The `nx`/`ny`/`fast_axis`/`rev_*` arguments must match the
`rasterize` call that produced the sweep.

### `random_ngon_vertices(n)` → `(n, 2)` vertices
A random simple-ish n-gon, for tests/demos.

23-
24-- **`field(target)` blocks**: issues the setpoint, polls `is_ramping` until
25:  clear, then a `settle_s` dwell (default 3 s). The set-point is **not**
26-  retrievable as a field — get always returns the measurement; never infer
27-  field from the last set call. Last commanded target is stashed at
28-  `commanded_field` (property).
29:- Non-blocking path: **`start_field_ramp(target)`** issues and returns
30-  immediately; pair with **`wait_for_ramp(timeout=None, tol=None)`** (poll the
31:  ramp flag, then settle — flat `settle_s` if `tol is None`, else poll the
32-  readback to within `tol` Tesla; `timeout=None` auto-bounds from `|ΔB|/slew`,
33-  `math.inf` waits forever). This enables measure-while-ramping.
34-- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: the ramp is commanded before the wait; a kernel
35-  interrupt leaves the supply ramping to its last target. Recovery is calling
36:  `field()`/`start_field_ramp()` again — there is no abort method.
37-- Limit: `max_field_T = 14.0`; targets beyond it (or beyond the `field`
38-  validator) raise before any setpoint is sent (checked on both the blocking
39-  and non-blocking paths).

41-  field-matching check), `output_enabled()`, `persistent_switch_on()` (reads);
42:  `status()` prints a summary. `start_field_ramp` raises if the persistent
43-  switch is off or the output is disabled.

140-  (ground) and 9 (through) are reserved. Constructor validates ranges and
141-  rejects duplicate line/tap numbers.

143-  contact(s)). Make-before-break against ground: grounds every managed line and
144-  opens its taps, closes the target `(line, tap)` relays, then opens the
145-  grounds (routed lines go live, unused lines float), then settles. **It grounds
146-  every managed line mid-transition** — ramp any DC source wired through the mux
147-  to 0 first.

149-  routing.

152-  pair keys and `"sr0": "drain current on …"` when ports follow the
153-  `source`/`drain`/`srN±` naming convention.
154:- Properties: `settle_s`, `routing` (last selected). Operates only on managed
155-  lines and never calls `qsw.reset()`.
156-
157-Module helper `target_state(lines, breakouts, routing)` → sorted `(line, tap)`

"""Raw look at SdH spot checks runs 6 (e-side, 0->10 T) and 7 (h-side, 10->0.3 T): R(B), R(1/B), stats."""
import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run, resolve_channels
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 8))
for k, rid in enumerate((6, 7)):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}")
    print(summarize_run(r))
    ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain
    R = (r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I
    T = r.col("T_sample")
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R, I, T = B[o], R[o], I[o], T[o]
    print(f"run {rid}: {len(B)} pts, B {B.min():.3f}..{B.max():.3f}, dB med {np.median(np.diff(B))*1e3:.1f} mT; R {R.min():.1f}..{R.max():.1f} Ohm; "
          f"R(B<0.1)={np.median(R[B<0.35]):.1f}; I {I.min()*1e9:.2f}..{I.max()*1e9:.2f} nA; T {T.min():.3f}..{T.max():.3f} K; interrupted {r.interrupted}")
    ax[k, 0].plot(B, R, "-", lw=0.8); ax[k, 0].set_xlabel("B (T)"); ax[k, 0].set_ylabel("Rxx B_1-B_2 (Ohm)"); ax[k, 0].set_title(f"run {rid} raw R(B)")
    m = B > 1.0
    ax[k, 1].plot(1 / B[m], R[m], "-", lw=0.8); ax[k, 1].set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax[k, 1].set_ylabel("Rxx (Ohm)"); ax[k, 1].set_title(f"run {rid} R(1/B), B>1 T")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/raw_spot_6_7.png", dpi=100); print("saved")
EOF

"""SdH read of spot checks 6 (e, n=+3.2e12) and 7 (h, n=-1.2e12): sdh_onset tones + sdh_fft spectrum, vs Luttinger F_L."""
import numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg"); import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, resolve_channels, sdh_fft, sdh_onset, luttinger_frequency
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 8))
for k, (rid, n12) in enumerate(((6, 3.2), (7, -1.2))):
    r = open_run(f"data/{rid}"); ch = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    B = r.col("magnet_field"); I = r.col("sr0_X") / ch["sr0"].gain; R = np.abs((r.col("sr1_X") / ch["sr1"].gain) / I)
    o = np.argsort(B); B, R = B[o], R[o]
    FL = luttinger_frequency(abs(n12) * 1e16)
    print(f"\n=== run {rid}: n = {n12:+.1f}e12 -> F_L(full density, 4-fold) = {FL:.1f} T; F_L/2 = {FL/2:.1f}, F_L/4 = {FL/4:.1f}")
    try:
        on = sdh_onset(R, B, b_lo=0.5, r_full_scale=50e-6 / 10e-9)
        print(on.summary())
    except Exception as e:
        print("sdh_onset:", type(e).__name__, e)
    for lo, hi in ((1.0, 10.0), (2.0, 10.0), (4.0, 10.0)):
        m = (B >= lo) & (B <= hi)
        f, sp = sdh_fft(R[m][:, None], B[m], nfft=2048, bg_degree=5, log=False)
        sp = sp[0]; sel = f > 2
        pk = np.argsort(sp[sel])[::-1][:6]
        print(f"  FFT window {lo}-{hi} T: top peaks (T: amp) " + ", ".join(f"{f[sel][p]:.1f}:{sp[sel][p]:.2g}" for p in sorted(pk, key=lambda p: f[sel][p])))
        if lo == 1.0:
            ax[k, 1].plot(f, sp, label=f"{lo}-{hi} T")
        else:
            ax[k, 1].plot(f, sp, alpha=0.6, label=f"{lo}-{hi} T")
    ax[k, 1].axvline(FL, color="k", ls="--", lw=0.8, label=f"F_L {FL:.1f} T"); ax[k, 1].axvline(FL / 2, color="gray", ls=":", lw=0.8)
    ax[k, 1].set_xlim(0, 80); ax[k, 1].set_xlabel("SdH frequency (T)"); ax[k, 1].legend(fontsize=7); ax[k, 1].set_title(f"run {rid} FFT (linear R, poly5 bg)")
    # detrended trace vs 1/B
    m = B >= 1.0
    bg = np.polyval(np.polyfit(B[m], R[m], 5), B[m])
    ax[k, 0].plot(1 / B[m], R[m] - bg, lw=0.7); ax[k, 0].set_xlabel("1/B (1/T)"); ax[k, 0].set_ylabel("dR (Ohm)"); ax[k, 0].set_title(f"run {rid} detrended, B>1 T")
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig("hera_scratch/sdh_spot_6_7.png", dpi=100); print("saved")
EOF

"""PreToolUse hook: the episode ends when the agent hands a measure cell to the
rig, or settles in to wait for it.

Installed by `hera-replay cut` as <session>/.claude/episode_stop.py. The
handoff itself is the nb-collab stub's business (it lands the append, never
executes, and writes <session>/episode-stop.json); the hera-watch stub writes
the same marker. This hook denies any ScheduleWakeup / Monitor call (in the
live sessions those only ever follow a handoff) and records it as the marker.
Once the marker exists, every later Bash / ScheduleWakeup / Monitor call (the
matcher's tools) is denied and ends the turn (`continue: false`), so
`claude -p` exits on its own with its result event. One exception: after the
watch arms (on the first code cell appended, which may be a prep cell), the
one Bash call that appends to the measure notebook goes through, so the cell
the watch was armed for lands.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import shlex
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone

HEREDOC_BODY = re.compile(r"<<\s*-?\s*(['\"]?)(\w+)\1[^\n]*\n.*?\n\2[ \t]*(?=\n|$)", re.DOTALL)
MEASURE_SUFFIX = "_measure.ipynb"
WAIT_TOOLS = ("ScheduleWakeup", "Monitor")


def appends_to_measure(command):
    """Whether a Bash command has an `nb-collab append` naming a measure notebook."""
    stripped = HEREDOC_BODY.sub("<<HEREDOC", command).replace("\\\n", " ")
    lexer = shlex.shlex(stripped, posix=True, punctuation_chars="();<>|&\n")
    lexer.whitespace = " \t\r"
    lexer.whitespace_split = True
    try:
        tokens = list(lexer)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    for i, tok in enumerate(tokens[:-1]):
        if tok == "nb-collab" and tokens[i + 1] == "append":
            j = i + 2
            while j < len(tokens) and not set(tokens[j]) <= set(lexer.punctuation_chars):
                if tokens[j].endswith(MEASURE_SUFFIX):
                    return True
                j += 1
    return False


def stop_output(reason: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "continue": False,
        "stopReason": reason,
        "hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
            "permissionDecision": "deny",
            "permissionDecisionReason": reason,
        },
    }


def main() -> int:
    payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
    root = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or payload.get("cwd") or os.getcwd()
    marker = os.path.join(root, "episode-stop.json")
    tool = payload.get("tool_name")
    tool_input = payload.get("tool_input") or {}
    if os.path.exists(marker):
        with open(marker, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            record = json.load(fh)
        if (tool == "Bash" and record.get("tool") == "hera-watch" and "append_pass" not in record
                and "append_landed" not in record and appends_to_measure(tool_input.get("command", ""))):
            record["append_pass"] = payload.get("tool_use_id")
            with open(marker, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                json.dump(record, fh, indent=2)
            return 0
        json.dump(stop_output("episode complete"), sys.stdout)
        return 0
    if tool not in WAIT_TOOLS:
        return 0
    record = {
        "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "tool": tool,
        "command": json.dumps(tool_input),
        "invocation": tool,
        "cell_ids": [],
        "tool_use_id": payload.get("tool_use_id"),
    }
    with open(marker, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(record, fh, indent=2)
    json.dump(stop_output("episode complete"), sys.stdout)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# vti-02 stacking-order campaign — plan (living)

Goal: ABAB vs ABCA vs ABCB, region-resolved (one measured pair: sr1 = B_1−B_2),
evidence-cited, or a calibrated "cannot tell". Envelope: TG [−0.3, +1.0], BG [−1.3, +2.0],
Si [−25, +25] V (unused), |B| ≤ 10 T, T ≤ 100 K. Base T ≈ 1.2 K, T_e ≈ 8 K.

## Discriminants (what each stacking predicts on this rig)
- **ABAB (Bernal)** — two bilayer-like parabolic bands (light + heavy), semimetallic
  overlap at CNP, small D-tunable gap. Fan: two interpenetrating 4-fold LL ladders
  (crossings), gaps at total ν = 4k near CNP; 16-fold zero mode → first strong gaps at
  ν = ±8 (±4 weaker, symmetry-broken).
- **ABCA (rhombohedral)** — one quartic band, large DOS at CNP; strongly D-gapped
  (R_CNP grows without saturating, many kΩ → MΩ at 0.25 V/nm); often correlated
  insulator at D = 0. Fan: a single ladder, no crossings; 16-fold zero mode
  (N = 0..3 orbitals), first gaps ν = ±8/±4 with orbital splittings.
- **ABCB (mixed)** — Dirac-like (monolayer-like) band + bilayer-like parabolic band,
  semimetal with small D gap. Fan: a Dirac ladder (gaps at ν_D = 4(N+½): ±2, ±6, ±10…)
  interleaved with a 4k ladder; 12-fold zero mode → ν = ±6 first gaps.

## Steps
1. **Gate C liveness** (`gate-current-sanity-check`, runs 0–3) — DONE. Alive on the
   provided pair, Rxx 60–330 Ω, gate currents at pA floor to the limits. Two peaks per
   gate leg (two CNP ridges).
2. **0 T gatemap + (n, D) calibration** (`gatemap`, run 4 aborted/railed, run 5) — DONE.
   Ridge A: slope −0.773 → c_bg/c_tg = 0.773 (prior 0.864); c_tg anchored at 9.5 nm
   prior (absolute scale UNVERIFIED); n_offset −0.089e12; D_offset −0.013 V/nm from
   R_CNP(D) vertex. R_CNP 240 Ω at D = 0 → 2.4 kΩ at D = 0.25 V/nm, saturating —
   small D gap, argues against ABCA but is not a stacking read alone. Ridge B: a
   parallel region electron-doped by 0.43e12 (series mosaic; expect shadow lines
   shifted by +0.43e12 in the fan).
3. **SdH spot checks** (`sdh-spot-check`, run 6 e-side n = +3.2e12 0→10 T; run 7
   h-side n = −1.2e12 10→0.3 T) — DONE. Oscillations from ~1 T; R→0 QH minima at
   5.92/7.16 T (run 6), 1.68/2.04 T (run 7). Minima are NOT one 1/B-periodic ladder;
   ν assignment is ambiguous at the ±8 % level of the unverified scale. FFTs are
   dominated by the non-oscillatory jump at 7.5–8 T (run 6) — combs at the window
   resolution, not tones. Read: multi-band LL structure; the fan is the decisive read.
4. **Landau fan at D = 0** (`landau-fan`, NEXT) — n fast along the D = 0 line
   (−1.28 … +3.26e12, TG-limited both ends, 100 pts), B slow 1 → 10 T in 100 mT
   (91 rows), sr1 100 µV. Establishes: (a) absolute ν per LL line from slopes
   dn/dB = νe/h → the lever-arm (absolute n scale) check the calibration lacks;
   (b) the zero-mode degeneracy from the lowest gaps emanating from the CNP
   (ν = ±4/±8 vs ±6 vs ±2); (c) one ladder vs two interpenetrating ladders
   (crossings) vs Dirac+parabolic interleaving; (d) the region-B shadow (lines
   offset +0.43e12) as a control. ≈ 4 h 40 m, ends at 10 T.
   Checkpoints: first row (rail/leak/flat channel); ~3, 5, 7 T partial `fan_grids`
   re-form; abort on rail across many columns, leak trip, T > 1.5 K, or no LL
   structure by 5 T.
5. **Conditional follow-ups** (choose from step-4 data; magnet rides 10 → low B):
   a. Fan at finite D (D ≈ +0.2 V/nm, same n line where inside the box): ABAB —
      LL crossings move, gap at CNP; ABCB — Dirac gap opens; ABCA — insulating.
   b. T-dependence of the lowest-ν gaps (set_both ≤ 100 K, ratio 0.95) only if the
      zero-mode degeneracy read is ambiguous (gap hierarchy vs T).
   c. If the ν assignment is still ambiguous, a 1/B-uniform high-resolution cut at a
      fixed n where two ladders are distinct.
6. **Verdict** in the ana notebook per the output contract (per-region line for the
   B_1−B_2 pair; evidence with run ids; hedges).

## What would change my mind
- A single clean ladder with no crossings and huge R_CNP at high B → ABCA (despite the
  small D gap at 0 T).
- ν = ±6 as the first CNP gap, or a 4(N+½) ladder coexisting with a 4k ladder → ABCB.
- Two ladders with crossings, gaps at ν = 4k, first at ±8 → ABAB.
- Fan lines extrapolating to n ≠ 0 at B = 0 → the CNP/n_offset or scale is off:
  recalibrate before any ν read.
- Region-B shadow lines confusing the ladder count → weight lines by amplitude and
  check the +0.43e12 offset before counting bands.

## Banned / out of scope
Extending gate limits; standalone Si survey; any safety-surface change.

The zeros are **not one 1/B-periodic ladder** (Δ(1/B) between successive minima 0.061, 0.040, 0.035, 0.064, 0.029 T⁻¹) — two ladders, or one ladder with a lifted degeneracy. Under the run-5 scale the two deep zeros sit at total ν ≈ 22.4 / 18.5 (a 4k+2 sequence, Dirac-like offset — the ABCB reading); an 8.7 % larger n puts them at ν = 24 / 20 (a 4k sequence — the ABAB/ABCA reading). The two are indistinguishable from a single cut because the absolute density scale is the geometry prior (c_tg from 9.5 nm hBN), unverified. The FFTs are **not tone spectra**: the 7.5–8 T jump survives the poly-5 detrend and produces combs at the window's 1/B resolution (2.5 T for 2–10 T, 6.7 T for 4–10 T); the tool's 7.2 T "tone" and its "harmonics" are that jump. **Run 7 (n = −1.2×10¹²):** deep minima at 1.68 T (12 Ω) and 2.04 T (14 Ω) with fast oscillations below 2 T and slow, large ones above (maxima 335 Ω at 2.45 T, 300 Ω at 4 T); minima 2.74, 3.38, 4.14, 4.92, 6.00, 6.94, 8.34 T → ν ≈ 18, 15, 12, 10, 8.3, 7.2, 6.0 under the run-5 scale — again not a single ladder; this close to the CNP a semimetal's second (heavier, opposite-sign) pocket is expected to interleave. That is plan step 4.

# === Landau fan on the D = 0 line (`landau-fan`): n fast [-1.28, +3.26]e12 (100 pts) x B slow 1 -> 10 T (100 mT, 91 rows) ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD
# --- session calibration from run 5 (cnp-and-dline-calibration; ratio data-calibrated, absolute scale = geometry prior) ---
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-03, c_bg=2.161e-03, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)

# --- preconditions (assumed, not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0, _B0 = T_sample(), magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (|B|<0.05: handoff left 0 T), V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (0), "
      f"nplci tg/bg = {k_tg.nplci()}/{k_bg.nplci()} (1/1), PS heater {magnet.persistent_switch_on()}, output {magnet.output_enabled()}")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5 and abs(_B0) < 0.05 and abs(k_si()) < 0.01
assert k_tg.nplci() == 1 and k_bg.nplci() == 1, "gate-current nplci not 1"
assert magnet.persistent_switch_on() and magnet.output_enabled()

# --- fast axis: the D = 0 line (region-A calibration), hole edge -> electron edge, both ends TG-limited ---
N_FAST = 100
_ns = np.linspace(-2, 4, 6001); _Vt, _Vb = calc_gate_voltages(_ns, 0.0, **CAL)
_ok = (_Vt >= TG_MIN) & (_Vt <= TG_MAX) & (_Vb >= BG_MIN) & (_Vb <= BG_MAX)
n_vec = np.linspace(_ns[_ok].min() + 0.005, _ns[_ok].max() - 0.005, N_FAST)          # 1e12 cm^-2
Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec = calc_gate_voltages(n_vec, 0.0, **CAL)
assert Vtg_vec.min() >= TG_MIN and Vtg_vec.max() <= TG_MAX and Vbg_vec.min() >= BG_MIN and Vbg_vec.max() <= BG_MAX, "fast line leaves the validator box"
assert len(Vtg_vec) == len(Vbg_vec) == N_FAST
_nchk, _Dchk = calc_nD(Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec, **CAL)
assert np.allclose(_nchk, n_vec) and np.abs(_Dchk).max() < 1e-6
print(f"fast line: n {n_vec[0]:+.3f} -> {n_vec[-1]:+.3f} e12 ({N_FAST} pts, dn {n_vec[1]-n_vec[0]:.4f}e12); "
      f"Vtg {Vtg_vec[0]:+.4f} -> {Vtg_vec[-1]:+.4f} V ({(Vtg_vec[1]-Vtg_vec[0])*1e3:.1f} mV), Vbg {Vbg_vec[0]:+.4f} -> {Vbg_vec[-1]:+.4f} V ({(Vbg_vec[1]-Vbg_vec[0])*1e3:.1f} mV)")

# --- slow axis: B 1 -> 10 T, 100 mT, ascending (magnet sits at 0; ends at the cap so the next step rides down) ---
B_vec = np.round(np.arange(1.0, 10.0001, 0.1), 4)
assert B_vec.max() <= B_SESSION_CAP and B_vec.min() > 0
FAST_DELAY, SLOW_DELAY = 1.0, 4.0     # 1 s/pt (run-5 calibrated 1.10 s/pt incl. reads); 4 s after the 1.3 V flyback (> 10 tau)
I_TRIP = 1e-9

# Fixed sensitivity for the whole fan: 100 uV = 10 kOhm FS at 10 nA. LL minima (tens of Ohm) sit at 0.2-0.5 % of FS,
# readable per run 5; only a CNP column > 10.9 kOhm at high B would rail, and that column is not what the read needs.
sr1.sensitivity(100e-6)
print(f"B grid: {len(B_vec)} rows, {B_vec[0]} -> {B_vec[-1]} T; drive {sr1.amplitude()} V -> 10 nA; sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V (10 kOhm FS); "
      f"sr0 sens {sr0.sensitivity()} V; tau {sr1.time_constant()} s / {sr1.filter_slope()} dB")

mc = dict(meas_config); mc["Si (V)"] = k_si(); mc["sample_temperature:"] = _T0
mc["comments"] = (f"landau-fan D=0: n {n_vec[0]:+.2f}..{n_vec[-1]:+.2f}e12 fast ({N_FAST} pts, co-swept Vtg/Vbg on the run-5 D=0 line), "
                  f"B 1->10 T slow 100 mT ({len(B_vec)} rows), sr1 100 uV, fast_delay {FAST_DELAY} s, base T, Vsi 0")
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('landau-fan')
s.add_comment(f'D = 0 line (run-5 cal: ratio {CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset {CAL["n_offset"]:+.3f}e12, D_offset {CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f} V/nm); '
              f'fast n {n_vec[0]:+.3f} -> {n_vec[-1]:+.3f} e12 cm^-2, {N_FAST} pts (Vtg {Vtg_vec[0]:+.3f}..{Vtg_vec[-1]:+.3f}, Vbg {Vbg_vec[0]:+.3f}..{Vbg_vec[-1]:+.3f} V); '
              f'slow B 1 -> 10 T, 100 mT, {len(B_vec)} rows; T = base; Vsi = 0; sr1 100 uV; fast_delay {FAST_DELAY} s, slow_delay {SLOW_DELAY} s')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg_vec[0]); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg_vec[0])
interruptible_sleep(10)

# row layout: [time, B(slow), Vtg(fast), Vbg(fast), T_sample, k_tg.curr, k_bg.curr, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr0.X)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)

def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[5])), abs(float(data[6]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f"LEAK TRIP at B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T, Vtg={float(data[2]):+.3f}, Vbg={float(data[3]):+.3f}: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A")
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

try:
    s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtg_vec, Vbg_vec],
                     slow_delay=SLOW_DELAY, fast_delay=FAST_DELAY)
finally:
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)    # gates parked; the field stays where the sweep left it (10 T on completion)
print(f"done: B = {magnet.field():+.3f} T, (Vtg, Vbg) = ({k_tg.volt():+.4f}, {k_bg.volt():+.4f}), T_sample = {T_sample():.3f} K")

The spot-check FFTs are window-resolution combs from the 7.5–8 T jump, not tones — logged as a METHOD note. `hera_scratch/plan.md` written (it was missing at pickup); session notes updated.

Priced ≈ 4 h 40 m from run-5's 1.10 s/pt. It breaks the ν degeneracy directly (LL-line slopes give ν and the lever arm independent of the calibration) and reads the stacking: two crossing 4k ladders / ν = ±8 (ABAB) vs one ladder + insulating CNP column (ABCA) vs interleaved 4(N+½) ladder / ν = ±6 (ABCB). Region-B shadow lines at +0.43×10¹² are the control.
